title: Hybrid-quant metadata sync and pinning strategy for model onboarding
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: produce a repeatable process and tooling to (1) ingest metadata for newly onboarded models that have multiple quantized variants (int8, nf4, q4_k_m), (2) ensure deterministic version pinning policy for customers, and (3) publish performance profiles to the catalog and docs.

Problem: Recent onboarding of mixed-precision variants exposed inconsistent metadata shapes (missing tokenization notes, different 'variant' naming, absent kernel/seq_length tags). This leads to incorrect performance profile publishing, broken version pinning in rollout configs, and confusion for tenants selecting optimal variants.

Scope:
- Define canonical metadata fields for hybrid quant variants (variant_id, base_model_ref, quant_scheme, expected_fp16/amp behavior, fallback_compatibility, kernel_preferences, typical_seq_distribution).
- Implement a metadata normalization step in the onboarding pipeline that reconciles vendor-supplied labels and normalizes names into the catalog taxonomy.
- Create a pinning policy that: (a) pins by model family + semantic version + quant_tag, (b) allows stable aliasing (e.g., `stable-int8-2025-02`) for customers, (c) records fallback variants when pinned variant is unavailable.
- Extend performance-profile publisher to emit separate profiles per variant and an aggregate family view for the catalog UI and SDK.
- Author docs + README for PMs/DS/SEs that explains trade-offs and how to pick variants for latency/cost/quality.

Non-goals: Building new quant kernels — out of scope. Long-term analytics for quality delta between variants (separate initiative).

Success criteria:
- Metadata linting detects >95% of inconsistent fields during onboarding.
- All newly onboarded hybrid-quant models have variant-level profile published within 48 hours of onboarding.
- Pinning policy documented and sample configs available in console (canary + stable).
comments: 2025-02-12 - Asha Patel: Kickoff notes. Ran quick audit of last 12 onboarded models; 7 had inconsistent 'quant' tags. Logged examples and attached spreadsheet.

2025-02-14 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented prototype normalizer that maps vendor tags (eg 'q4_k_m_v2', 'int8-v1') to canonical variant_id. Basic unit tests added; PR in flight: https://github.com/redwood-inference/catalog/pull/421
2025-02-16 - PM review (Sofia Li): Asked for explicit 'fallback_compatibility' field to be included to support runtime fallback routing. Added to schema proposal.
2025-02-18 - Design (Ravi Mehta): Requested example catalog UI rows demonstrating family-level view vs variant-level view. Raised spacing constraints for long kernel preference strings.
2025-02-20 - Ops (Tanya Gomez): Noted that pinning aliases need to be immutable once promoted to 'stable' unless a forced migration workflow is followed. Suggest audit log entry on alias change.
next_steps: Finish metadata normalizer PR and land unit tests
Add lint rules to onboarding pipeline to block merges with missing canonical fields
Implement pin alias API and audit log hook (backend + console endpoint)
Publish docs: canonical field reference, pinning FAQ, example YAML configs
Coordinate with Runtime team to annotate kernel_preferences in model artifacts
implementation_notes: Normalizer lives in catalog/ingest. It should be idempotent and produce a deterministic canonical name set. Pin aliases will be stored alongside model metadata with 'sealed' flag for stable promotion. Performance publisher will attach variant_id and a family_id to each profile. Use existing telemetry tags for seq_length buckets. Add an internal feature flag for rollout.
risks: Incorrect fallback mappings could cause higher latency if runtime routes to an incompatible variant
Overzealous linting may block urgent vendor-provided patches during onboarding
Alias immutability needs clear rollback path or customers may be surprised by changes
